item.title: Miami’s High-Priced QB Loses Top Target Before Notre Dame Clash
item.description: In some ways, it’s hard for Miami’s Malachi Toney to describe how close he’s grown to Darian Mensah in a matter of months. The quarterback-wide receiver combination is one of the most potent 1-2 punches in college football this season and is the main reason why the Hurricanes are the No. 1 team in the initial College Football Playoff rankings released on Tuesday. “It’s just been crazy,” Toney told reporters this week. “We were just in the locker room just talking about how I saw him at [Prime 112 Restaurant] right after he committed. Just him getting adapted to Miami, we’ve grown so close.” That connection was disrupted Wednesday, when Toney suffered an ankle injury in practice and underwent surgery. He’s expected back later this season, but will miss Saturday’s much-anticipated matchup with Notre Dame, No. 11 in the Playoff rankings. But confidence remains high in Coral Gables because Miami has Mensah, who’s proven himself as a leader and competitor within Miami’s program since he arrived. “He’s eager to get the ball,” Miami head coach Mario Cristobal said this week. “Enthusiasm, excited, doesn’t flinch, very focused. Just ready, prepared. It was a preparation to give him that kind of confidence. He’s ready to roll.” Mensah has emerged as one of college football’s biggest stars this season. He’s at his third school in three years, having led Duke to a win in the ACC championship game in 2025 and Tulane to a 9-4 record in 2024. This year he’s been one of the most impactful transfer portal additions in the sport–Mensah leads the nation in touchdown passes (25), and his 80.7% completion percentage would break the NCAA single-season record by more than three points (Bo Nix, 77.4%, 2023). Overall, Miami’s offense leads the nation in scoring at 46.7 points per game. Mensah’s ascension encapsulates how player mobility has changed the sport. Each transfer has led to a bigger on-field opportunity and higher compensation. Mensah arrived at Tulane as a consensus three-star recruit in 2023. He signed a two-year, $8 million deal with Duke in 2024 , one of the biggest in college football at that time. Today, his $6.5 million NIL valuation at Miami is the highest in men’s collegiate athletics, according to On3 . Mensah’s endorsement deals include CVS, Derby Watch Supply, Dr. Pepper, and SlingTV. Saturday’s game at Notre Dame was the predetermined biggest game for Mensah and Miami this season, and Toney’s injury has scaled the challenge by a significant margin. Toney, like Mensah, is a nationwide leader in receiving; he ranks first in catches (73), receiving touchdowns (13), and is second in receiving yards (1,027). Saturday’s game is a huge opportunity for Mensah to showcase his ability without his top weapon. It’s a game that’s been circled for NFL scouts, who’ve been waiting for Mensah to perform against an elite team, and in a primetime slot. item.title: NFL viewership stabilizes after early-season declines as league nears midway point
item.description: Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images After some viewership declines during the early portion of the season, the NFL is back on track. Entering Week 9, NFL viewership is up 3% year-over-year, according to a report by Austin Karp in Sports Business Journal . That increase is within the range that could be entirely attributed to Nielsen’s recent methodological changes that altered how the company measured co-viewing , the act of multiple people viewing one telecast in the same room. A recent report by The Athletic’s Stewart Mandel suggested Nielsen’s recent changes raised baseline college football viewership by 3.4% . It’s unclear if the NFL is seeing a similar lift, however. It’s important to note that the league came out publicly against Nielsen’s changes before the seas0n began. NFL telecasts are averaging 18.4 million viewers through Week 8. The two top audiences of the year both belong to the Kansas City Chiefs and CBS. Chiefs-Raiders averaged 28.45 million viewers on the network in October, and last weekend’s Chiefs-Broncos game averaged 28.18 million viewers. Fox holds the next two most-watched contests; Commanders-Cowboys in September (27.21 million viewers) and 49ers-Seahawks in October (26.70 million viewers). Per Karp, CBS is up 5% overall through Week 8, averaging 19.6 million viewers. Thursday Night Football on Prime Video also continues to trend up, averaging 17.6 million viewers per game. Each of its seven telecasts have seen year-over-year gains. ESPN’s Monday Night Football is up 22% versus last year, though it’s unclear if that number is buoyed by last year’s doubleheaders, which depressed ESPN’s per-game average and would make for a more favorable comparison. Figures for Fox’s and NBC’s viewership through Week 8 were not published. In data released to reporters on Thursday, the NFL pointed towards the number of close games as helping viewership this season. 71 games have been decided by one-score margins so far this season, tied with 2022 for the most in NFL history through eight weeks. 38 games have had a game-winning score in the final five minutes or overtime, tied with 2021 for the most through eight weeks. The NFL sent along some interesting stats this AM: •71 games have been decided by one score (8 or fewer points) – tied with 2022 for the most through Week 8 in NFL history. •38 games have featured a game-winning score in the final five minutes of the 4th quarter or OT – tied with 2021 for the most through Week 8 in NFL history. Closer games means higher viewership numbers. — Richard Deitsch (@richarddeitsch) November 5, 2026 Be it close games, Nielsen changes, or just normal viewership fluctuations, the league likes when ratings go up. And so far this season, the NFL continues to display its strength in viewership. item.title: Arsenal star told why he should consider Bundesliga move
item.description: Arsenal star told why he should consider Bundesliga move Martin Odegaard has been linked with a potential move to Bayern Munich , with the Arsenal captain being advised to consider joining the German giants if an opportunity arises. The Norwegian has established himself as one of the most important players in Mikel Arteta’s squad. He wears the captain’s armband at Arsenal and also leads his country’s national team, underlining his importance at both club and international level. Arsenal have no intention of selling Odegaard or any of their key players, meaning Bayern would face a difficult task if they wanted to bring him to the Bundesliga. The midfielder also appears happy in North London, having produced several impressive performances since becoming an important part of the team. However, reports suggest he could be open to considering a move to Bayern , one of Europe’s leading clubs. Eivind Bisgaard Sundet believes the switch would make sense for the Arsenal captain and has explained why he could benefit from the change. Bayern Munich viewed as a good fit Odegaard’s technical ability and creativity could make him an attractive option for Bayern, particularly given the style of football the German side plays. You’d have more possession.” Sundet clearly sees Bayern as a club where Odegaard could remain influential while benefiting from a different style of football and schedule. item.title: David Ferrer suggested to become Carlos Alcaraz’s new coach soon, ‘I would not be surprised’
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz’s steady return to fitness has belied his rapid return to form, which has been almost instant since he played his first competitive match back at the US Open in September. Since then, the Spaniard has already won two ATP titles and is currently into the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters . Given how ravaged the field in the French capital is, it feels like there is nobody left capable of stopping him from adding a new piece of silverware to his already sprawling cabinet. And yet, as he silently moves through the draw and closer to his first Paris Masters title, it is Jannik Sinner and Ben Shelton who have been dominating headlines. After all, their respective coaching changes both came as great surprises, and have sparked mass speculation about how Carlos Alcaraz might react. Brad Gilbert backs Carlos Alcaraz to make coaching change Speaking on the latest Big T podcast , it was Brad Gilbert who shared his theory for what the future might hold for Alcaraz. After all, since Juan Carlos Ferrero departed his team around this time last year, he has made no major additions to replace him, instead trusting in the guidance of Samu Lopez to spearhead his development. Discussing Ben Shelton ’s decision to add Alcaraz’s old coach to his team, Gilbert actually made a bold prediction about the seven-time Grand Slam champion, noting: “I’m sure he’s eager to get to work and make some changes so he can close the gap on Sinner, Alcaraz, and Zverev, and his combined record against the three is not that great. “But honestly, I do believe now after what Sinner did, you know… I expect at least two, three, more guys in the top ten to make big changes, and I expect two, three, women, probably, that are playing the year-end championships, to make changes. “I think, actually, Alcaraz will make a move soon, and the guy to keep most eyes on, I think, is David Ferrer. “Because he’s all of a sudden stopping as the Davis Cup captain. Everyone thinks now that that’s a perfect solution to go to Jodar, but, you know, I would not be surprised if Alcaraz makes a move this off-season.” Elsewhere, Alcaraz recently discussed shock losses to Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev at the Paris Masters , as he seeks his first-ever title here. Chris Eubanks reacts to Ben Shelton hiring Juan Carlos Ferrero Shelton’s decision to hire Ferrero came completely out of left field, catching everyone by surprise. Chris Eubanks was no different, and chatting in that same podcast, he offered his honest view on the decision. “It completely caught me off guard as well,” the American admitted. He continued: “I’m sitting here kind of in this bit of a limbo period of wondering, who’s he gonna go with? Jodar seemed like the most logical choice, young Spaniard; he’s had success obviously with another young Spaniard. That’s kind of where I kind of think all my energy went towards. “And yesterday, you start to see the reports, and I go, this is actually a perfect match. Photo by Leonardo MUNOZ

item.title: Valencia manager could field a five-man defence to stop Real Madrid in La Liga clash
item.description: Valencia manager could field a five-man defence to stop Real Madrid in La Liga clash Real Madrid are set to travel to Mestalla to face Valencia this weekend as they look to extend their winning streak to eight games. Jose Mourinho’s team are flying high on the confidence gained from their dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over AEK Athens . Los Blancos have proved to be an unstoppable attacking unit in recent weeks following some tactical tweaks from Jose Mourinho. Now, according to AS , Valencia manager Javier Aguirre is testing a five-man defence in training in an attempt to stop Real Madrid. Aguirre prepares a defensive reshuffle The Mexican manager has tested a back line consisting of Pablo Maffeo, Arnau Martinez, Pepelu, Cesar Tarrega and Jose Gaya. Arnau is said to be operating as the right-sided centre-back, while Maffeo and Gaya would occupy the wing-back positions. Valencia could field a five-man backline to stop Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre had already experimented with pairing Maffeo and Arnau against Elche, but the former operated in a much more advanced role. Against Real Madrid, though, Aguirre’s side will look to be as compact as possible defensively and prevent Los Blancos ‘ attackers from thriving. The proposed system is also said to feature Guido Rodriguez, Javi Guerra and youngster Aaron Mayol in midfield, with Arnaut Danjuma partnering Umar Sadiq in attack. The Nigerian recently scored Valencia’s winner against Elche and could return to the starting line-up against Madrid. A potential challenge for Real Madrid Valencia are always a difficult team to face at Mestalla , and they have become significantly more solid since Aguirre took over. This weekend would mark Real Madrid’s final league visit to the stadium, with Valencia set to move to a new stadium next season. Jose Mourinho’s men will face a stern test against Valencia at the Mestalla. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre’s approach appears designed to restrict Madrid’s attacking space, particularly in wide areas, while maintaining three central defenders to deal with Kylian Mbappe. For Mourinho’s men, breaking down such a deep block would require creativity and the likes of Arda Guler and Jude Bellingham to find a way through. With Vinicius Jr. still unavailable through suspension, Mourinho should have no problem playing the Turkish international against Valencia. A five-man defence would provide a new kind of challenge for Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, and it remains to be seen how they fare this weekend.

item.title: Joan Garcia opens up on adapting to Barcelona’s style: ‘I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper’
item.description: Joan Garcia opens up on adapting to Barcelona’s style: ‘I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper’ Being a goalkeeper for Barcelona is about more than just stopping shots. It is one of the most demanding roles in football. Playing in goal for Hansi Flick’s Barça is a whole other story. The goalkeeper must act as the last defender on a number of occasions and remain alert to the space behind the back line. Joan Garcia has embraced those responsibilities since arriving from Espanyol in 2025. He has emerged as the perfect goalkeeper for Flick’s Barcelona. More than a shot-stopper Speaking in an interview with GQ, the 25-year-old discussed his adaptation to Barcelona, his development as a goalkeeper and how he manages the pressure of representing the club. “I have always felt very comfortable helping the team in that aspect. It is true that at Barcelona it is much more necessary, and it is something I enjoy working on and practising to keep improving every day,” Garcia said. (h/t SPORT ). “I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper. I try to help in many aspects of the game and remain very alert to anticipate and prevent possible chances for the opposition,” he added. Joan Garcia kept his first clean sheet in the Champions League at Barcelona. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) These qualities are very valuable to Flick’s Barcelona. Joan has repeatedly timed his rushes off the line to perfection. He recently celebrated his first Champions League clean sheet for the Catalan club in Barcelona’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa. Garcia on handling pressure and mental preparation The Spanish international has also spoken about the psychological demands of goalkeeping, where one mistake can define a player. “It is something we goalkeepers live with from a very young age. We know the position carries enormous responsibility, but it is not something that affects me too much,” he explained. “Over the years, I have learned to manage these situations much better and, at certain moments, I have worked with psychologists. At this elite level, I believe taking care of the mental side is fundamental.” Joan Garcia is slowly entering the scheme of things in the Spain squad. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Despite being only 25, Garcia also recognises his responsibility towards Barcelona’s younger players. “I try to contribute my experience, help and advise my teammates in whatever way I can, even though I am only 25 years old,” he said. The former Espanyol shot-stopper has also entered the reckoning for Spain under Luis de la Fuente, although a starting berth seems far-fetched. Joan Garcia has performed exceedingly well in the season and a half since he joined the club in 2025. It remains to be seen how the 25-year-old develops and whether he can be the goalkeeper who brings the Champions League back to the Spotify Camp Nou.

item.title: BCCI announces major venue change for India-Sri Lanka series; 1st ODI moved from New Delhi
item.description: The opening ODI of India's upcoming home series against Sri Lanka has been shifted from Delhi to Visakhapatnam, with the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirming the venue change on Thursday. The December 13 fixture, originally scheduled to be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, will now take place at the ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Visakhapatnam. Why has India vs Sri Lanka 1st ODI been shifted? The DDCA had approached the BCCI seeking a change in venue, citing its inability to host the international fixture amid renovation work and unfavourable weather conditions expected in Delhi during December. The association was concerned that the ongoing work at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, coupled with the possibility of weather-related disruptions, could affect the smooth organisation of the match. The BCCI subsequently approved the request and confirmed Visakhapatnam as the new venue for the series opener. India vs Sri Lanka: Revised ODI and T20I schedule Sri Lanka are scheduled to play three ODIs and three T20Is during their tour of India in December 2026. While the opening ODI has been moved to Visakhapatnam, the remaining five fixtures will continue at their previously allotted venues. The three-match ODI series will begin on December 13, followed by the T20I leg, which gets underway on December 22. item.title: Maraad Watson’s touchdown showed how far he has come at Texas
item.description: Maraad Watson made it 61 yards to the end zone . Steve Sarkisian kept talking about what happened once he got there. BIG MAN GOLD 😤 pic.twitter.com/bW3XZekWht — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 1, 2026 After Watson returned a fumble for a touchdown in the 31-3 win over Mississippi State on Saturday, his teammates joined him for a dance in the end zone. Sarkisian showed the play to his team Monday . The response around Watson was part of what he wanted to recognize. “What I loved about it was if you noticed his teammates when he scored, how many of them got to him to do his little dance in the end zone with him, and that’s the stuff you love as a coach,” Sarkisian said. “Maraad wasn’t beating his own chest when he got in the end zone. He turned and wanted to celebrate with his teammates, and so I think that speaks to who he is as a teammate, as a person, and he’s playing at a really high level.” The junior defensive tackle transferred from Syracuse in spring 2025 . Sarkisian remembers a reserved newcomer adjusting to a different city and program. item.title: “I need to improve” – Chelsea summer signing makes honest admission
item.description: “I need to improve” – Chelsea summer signing makes honest admission Marco Palestra Admits Chelsea Improvement Needed After Breakthrough Start Chelsea paid around £45 million for Marco Palestra in the summer, and that fee brings scrutiny. That is how it works at Stamford Bridge. Promise matters, versatility matters, pedigree matters, but sooner or later it comes down to performance. The 21-year-old arrived from Atalanta as the first signing of the Xabi Alonso era and, after an injury-hit start to the season, finally made his first competitive start in Chelsea’s 2-0 Premier League win over Manchester United. It was a useful step forward, even if it was not flawless. There were doubts from parts of the support over his defensive positioning against 10-man United. Fair enough. Full-backs and wing-backs at this level are judged brutally when they switch off. Still, Chelsea kept a clean sheet and that has not happened often enough at home in the league, especially in a win. Palestra sets clear Chelsea target Palestra himself was refreshingly direct about where he stands. “I was just happy because, when I was young, I never thought I could be a Chelsea player,” he said. “So the first emotion was only happiness. Now I am still happy, but I need to improve myself to win with this team.” That is the correct line. No noise, no self-congratulation, no empty talk. He knows ability got him here, and improvement will decide whether he stays in the side. Position switch changed career path Palestra also pointed to a key moment in his development. “When I was a bit older, like 16, our coach changed my position,” Palestra said. “His name is Marco Fioretto. He was the first one who moved me from midfield to out wide and he maybe changed my career.” Photo IMAGO It explains plenty. Players converted from midfield often read possession well, though defensive spacing out wide can take time. That seems to be the case here. Chelsea test awaits against Sunderland Chelsea now head to Sunderland, bottom of the table, and Alonso may well keep faith with him. The challenge for Palestra is simple, build on the clean sheet, sharpen the defending, and turn a decent first start into something more convincing.

item.title: LIV Backer Scraps 2027 League Plan After Player Shortfall
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images LIV Golf’s dream of a fresh start in 2027 has hit a hard wall. The financial backer behind the league, BC Partners Credit, has decided to scrap plans for a new version of the tour called “LIV 2.0.” The move comes after the group realized they could not secure enough player support to make the venture viable. According to reports, this decision marks a major blow to the league’s survival strategy just as it navigates Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings. The collapse of this plan means the league will likely face liquidation of its assets rather than a reboot. The stakes were high for this proposed revival. Up to $300 million was pledged by BC Partners Credit to finance the new structure. This funding was intended to support at least 10 tournaments with a heavy emphasis on team play and equity for the players. LIV CEO Scott O’Neil had previously touted the equity component as a “second bite of the apple” for golfers looking to build long-term value. However, the math simply didn’t work without the right talent. Although LIV was thought to have up to 30 players ready to remain with the league, the group lacked the requisite star power to warrant the investment. Public support for the new model was declared by only four players, among them Brendan Steele and Cameron Tringale. Ted Goldthorpe, a partner and head of BC Partners Credit, had expressed optimism earlier in the year. Speaking at a Sportico conference in September, he noted, “A lot of the money that was spent created the ecosystem and infrastructure that exists today. We think we can run this in a financially sustainable way because much of that spending went to getting the players, and the players are here.” Those hopes have now faded. Bankruptcy Court Shifts Focus The failure of the LIV 2.0 proposal changes the immediate legal landscape for the organization. Jon Rahm’s contract release occurred via a deal set for approval during a Thursday hearing at the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in New Jersey. Following the demise of the new funding plan, The Financial Times reported that this hearing will now center on LIV seeking asset liquidation. LIV Golf officials offered no immediate comment when asked about the final decision. Administrative changes are already underway as the league prepares for the end. On Wednesday, LIV Golf New Jersey submitted a request to change its address within the bankruptcy court. The new site shifts from a New York office to a commercial office property in Claymont, Delaware. This administrative shuffle often precedes the final dissolution of a company’s operations. The roots of this financial crisis trace back to the league’s launch in 2022 by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia. item.title: CAS defends Russian ice hockey ruling as Putin weighs in
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Russian President Vladimir Putin in action during a Night Hockey League friendly match at the skating rink in the Red Square. (is associated with: «CAS defends Russian ice hockey ruling as Putin weighs in») -/Kremlin/dpa The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has defended its decision to permit Russia to compete again in ice hockey world championships, saying bosses of the sport failed to prove the risk and did not sufficiently understand the legal situation. Politicians, sponsors and ice hockey bodies reacted with anger to the CAS decision on Friday. The International Olympic Committee lifted a ban on the Russian Olympic Committee in July, but it is being left up to individual sporting bodies if and how Russia is reincorporated, despite the Ukraine war still raging after four years. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) opted to continue to exclude Russian teams on security grounds, but Russia appealed to the world's top sports court and won. The ruling has implications for other sports. "The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) acknowledges the divisive reaction to the ruling," an unusual CAS statement said on Thursday. "CAS wishes to reiterate that as an independent sports arbitration institution, rulings are made on the legal substance of an appeal and on the sole basis of the arguments and evidence submitted by the Parties." The men's world championship takes place in Germany in May and sponsors are mulling withdrawal while Germany is considering handing back hosting rights. Top ice hockey nations, including world champions Finland, say they will boycott games against Russia. CAS said the IIHF could not back up its assertion that security concerns should prevent Russia's return. "The CAS Panel found that the IIHF did not present sufficient evidence to establish the legal requirements for the non-participation of Russian teams. The CAS Panel remarked that internal processes within the IIHF had previously raised this concern, the statement added. CAS would have considered a different ruling requesting that Russia competed as a neutral nation or some other nuance, but alleged the IIHF never asked for such a decision. "CAS cannot impose measures that have not been requested by the Parties," it said. Canada is hosting the under-20 world championship at the end of the year and Prime Minister Mark Carney has inferred Russian players will not receive visas. Germany may follow suit. The IIHF has been in crisis talks this week having said it was "surprised" by the CAS ruling. Russian President Vladimir Putin has become involved, telling government representatives on Thursday that countries are not willing to honour commitments they once made regarding sport. He accused them of imposing political restrictions on Russian athletes, which he described as a gross violation.

Given the Reds had dominated the defending league champions for long stretches and would have won without an extremely controversial non-penalty call, there was actually a case it was one of their best performances so far under new head coach Andoni Iraola. Then came Fenerbahce on Wednesday. When rather than taking out any frustrations over the weekend’s result on an opponent that looked overmatched on paper, Liverpool appeared less energetic, less motivated, and less effective. “Everyone looked disappointed and they should be disappointed,” captain Virgil van Dijk said after the match, which ended 3-2 in favour of their Turkish opponents. “We cannot lose in the manner we did, but it is down to Fenerbahce as well. But as a group have to go through good moments—but also less good moments. We switched off and weren’t ready for the first and second balls, so it’s a tough one to take.” If there’s one silver lining, it’s that with two games a week most weeks there’s never much time to dwell on things or a too long wait to put things right, and Liverpool head to London on Sunday to take on Crystal Palace knowing three points will soothe any concerns. “It’s massive,” Van Dijk added of the challenge Palace poses. “When we are preparing and recovering physically and mentally, we will be also looking forward. It’s always tough at Palace so I don’t expect anything different this time.”
